title: Event-sourcing engine, sign-up and sign-in
author: pratos with Claude Code
summary: People can sign up, sign in and sign out, and each of those is an event in the engine every later context will use. The engine stays small: optimistic appends, projections in the same transaction, one Sql port over four databases, and stories as tests.
current: cp-02 has the words and the design: `docs/DOMAIN-VOCABULARY.md` with Identity's Account and Sign-in, `packages/schema`, the vocabulary check, the plan room map and the event design. There is no engine, no domain package and no table yet.
discoveries: The Workers runtime caps PBKDF2 at 100,000 iterations; Web Crypto runs the same hashing in the Worker, in bun tests and in `just user-add`.
D1 has no interactive transactions, but a `batch` is atomic, which is all an append with its projection rows needs.
One stream per email (`account-<email>`), so two sign-ups racing for one email meet at the stream's version and the second is refused.
An unknown email is verified against a decoy hash, so it takes as long as a wrong password and gets the same answer.
D1 tables come from migrations, not `setup()`; a test checks that `0002_accounts.sql` holds exactly the DDL the engine and projection declare.
endState: Sign up at localhost:3000/signup and land signed in, your name in the header. `sign-up.snap.txt` reads as a story. `just agent-ready` reports one gap, the admin API, which cp-04 adds.
notDoing: An admin API or page; it arrives with the flags in cp-04.
Password reset, email confirmation or OAuth; the workshop needs none of them.
The Thread and Session deciders; the engine is ready for them, later stages add them.
Rate limiting sign-in; Cloudflare's rate-limiting rules can do it outside this code.
approach: Engine first, with its own tests, because every context will run on it. Then the account context as stories. Then the HTTP edge, seeds and pages, which only map onto it.

steps.caption: SignUp opens the account and records AccountOpened, never as an admin.
OpenAccount does the same for seeds and `just user-add`, and may set admin.
SignIn with a matching password records SignedIn for one device.
SignOut ends that device only; a second sign-out records nothing.

decisions.question: Sign-in: a library or our own?
decisions.why: Two tables and one hash function are small enough to read in one sitting. Ours runs on the engine like every other context, so a sign-up is an event with a story.

steps.caption: The browser posts an email and password to the API.
The API runs SignIn on the account's own stream in the engine.
The event and its projection row land in D1 together.
The browser keeps the token in a cookie scripts cannot read.
The library takes the request and answers it with its own handler.
It writes its own rows outside the event log, and calls a sign-in a session.

design.notes: Sign-in and sign-up are quiet, single-column pages met once a week. One dark action, refusals in a sentence, the product's own words.

phases.name: Engine: event store, one Sql port, stories
phases.goal: `packages/engine` appends against an expected version, writes projections in the same transaction, and runs unchanged on bun:sqlite, a Durable Object, D1 and Postgres.

changes.intent: Messages, deciders, `defineCommand` and `defineEvent`, rejections, and the given-when-then expect harness.
The one port every database implements; a unique-key violation becomes a WriteConflict.
One `stream_events` table, keyed by stream and version; `execute` retries a conflict three times.
`bunSqlite`, `durableObject`, `d1` (one atomic batch) and `postgres` layers for the Sql port.
`story(layer, dir)` runs steps on real SQL; each `then` lists exactly what that step appended.
On bun:sqlite and PGlite: same-write projections, stale appends conflict, failed projections roll back.

phases.name: Account context: sign up, sign in, sign out
phases.goal: The account decider turns the four commands into AccountOpened, SignedIn and SignedOut. Both stories pass and read as prose.

changes.intent: Hashing happens before decide; the decider sees a hash and whether it matched.

contract.code:
SignUp        = defineCommand('SignUp',        { accountId, email, name, passwordHash })
OpenAccount   = defineCommand('OpenAccount',   { accountId, email, name, admin, passwordHash }) // seeds, just user-add
SignIn        = defineCommand('SignIn',        { accountId, passwordMatched, tokenHash, expiresAt })
SignOut       = defineCommand('SignOut',       { accountId, tokenHash })
AccountOpened = defineEvent('AccountOpened',   { accountId, email, name, admin, passwordHash })
SignedIn      = defineEvent('SignedIn',        { accountId, tokenHash, expiresAt })
SignedOut     = defineEvent('SignedOut',       { accountId, tokenHash })
type AccountState = { kind: 'none' } | { kind: 'open'; accountId; passwordHash; signIns: string[] }
accountStream = (email) => `account-${email.trim().toLowerCase()}`

changes.intent: PBKDF2-SHA256 with Web Crypto and a constant-time compare; tokens stored only as SHA-256.
`accountsView`: the two tables, written in the same transaction as each event.
The `Accounts` service: decode, hash, execute on the account's stream, read the projection.
Two stories through the real engine on in-memory bun:sqlite, with a fixed clock.
The sign-up story, every hash printed as •••.

contract.code:
when   Sam signs up as sam@greenhouse.test
then   AccountOpened      sam by sam email="sam@greenhouse.test" name="Sam" admin=false passwordHash=•••
when   someone signs up again with SAM@greenhouse.test
then   rejected           an account with this email exists
when   Ana signs up with a short password
then   rejected           an email, a name, and a password of at least 12 characters

changes.intent: Wrong password and unknown email read alike; a second sign-out records nothing.
